heroHeadline: Hezbollah Launches 105-Wave Attack — Most Intense Day of War; Rubio: 'Pretty Solid Thing on the Table'; MoU Gives 60-Day Window; Shekel at 30+ Yr High; Bank of Israel Cuts Rates; Day 87
heroSubtitle: Day 87 (May 25): Hezbollah launched 105 attack waves against Israel — the highest single-day total since the conflict began and the most intense barrage of the war. Rockets struck Nahariya, killing one man and injuring 14. A drone also hit an area where IDF troops were operating in south Lebanon; cumulative Hezbollah attack waves reach 1,084+. On the diplomatic front, Secretary Rubio upgraded his language to 'pretty solid thing on the table,' confirming the emerging US-Iran MoU would provide a 60-day window to finalize terms and would commit Iran to never possessing a nuclear weapon — with nuclear enrichment details NOT in the initial MoU. Former CIA Director Petraeus said Iran is 'in the process of blinking' over Hormuz, citing Iran's restoration of 30 of 33 Hormuz missile sites. In the most significant financial confidence signal yet, the Bank of Israel cut interest rates 25bps to 3.75%, explicitly citing Iran deal progress; the Israeli shekel surged to a 30+ year high (~2.9 NIS/USD). US intelligence confirmed Iran has retained ~70% of its missile stockpile and could fully reconstitute in 6 months — adding urgency to negotiations. Israeli opposition leader Golan warned Israel is being sidelined, likely to 'learn the details of the agreement only after the fact.' Oil prices continued falling on deal momentum.
